svg.title: Add a stock comparison chart
svg.desc: Illustrated afternoon, 1 pm to 5 pm By hand. 5 messages from you. 1:00 pm, Your message. “Let me compare any stock with the S&P 500 in my stock market research app” 1:32 pm, Your message. The first chart shows prices in dollars. You ask for percentage gains so the lines are comparable. 1:55 pm, Your message. A stock appears to lose half its value overnight. You check the date and find a stock split. 2:10 pm, Your message. You ask the agent to test the math across the split and show you the expected numbers. 2:24 pm, Your message. You try a newly listed stock. The two lines start on different dates. You flag it and leave. 2:42 pm, Agent. “What should we show when the stock has less history than the index?” The agent waits. 5:00 pm, You return. You open the chat. The question has been waiting for over two hours. With 100x. 1 message from you. 1:00 pm, Your message. “Let me compare any stock with the S&P 500 in my stock market research app” 1:02 pm, You step away. You send it and leave. The agent builds the chart and checks the math. 1:08 pm, Agent. The agent plans a chart that starts both lines at 0% and shows how much each has moved. 2:50 pm, Agent. It tests a two-for-one split. A move from $100 to $50 on the split date shows 0% loss, as expected. 3:35 pm, Second model. The reviewer opens a newly listed stock and finds the index line starts five months earlier. 4:42 pm, Agent. It starts both lines on the first date they share, reruns the checks, and saves the chart and test results in the report. 5:00 pm, You return. You open the report and can verify the split math and the date both lines start.
